findings.F1: The tested situation stands out only in the rising calm profile. Wide (range at least 2 swings), low-close (bottom fifth) days there were followed by a next-day excess return of +2.98 % (t 3.38, 46 cases on 25 days). The same days in the other five profiles gave +0.89 % (t 0.67, chop agitated), −1.06 % (t −0.99, chop calm), +3.76 % (t 1.86, fall agitated), +0.21 % (t 0.19, fall calm) and +0.81 % (t 0.94, rise agitated). Calm and agitated were read here against the coin's median 30-day swing within folds B and C, not the past year's percentile.
findings.F2: The grading the idea claims is not in the bars. Across all wide low-close days, quartiles of width × nearness to the low gave next-day excess returns of +0.99 % (t 1.43), +1.55 % (t 2.42), +1.22 % (t 2.13) and +2.92 % (t 1.90), so only the top quartile is higher, and not reliably. Width terciles gave 3-day excess returns of +1.97 %, +2.75 % and +2.53 % (t 1.96, 2.20, 1.81), which do not grow with width. This matches step 5's failed supporting check.
findings.F3: In falling calm markets, wide days closing in the top fifth of their range were followed by a next-day excess return of −2.15 % (t −3.12, 40 cases, 26 days). This is the situation of the source brief 060 (falling calm high-close fade) and is already researched, so it is not a discovery.
findings.F4: Across all profiles, the decile of largest one-day falls scaled by the 30-day swing was followed by a next-day excess return of +1.07 % (t 2.37, 823 cases, 240 days). In the highest-volatility quartile, down days were followed by +1.07 % (t 2.32). This is the scaled-fall rebound the map already holds many times (falling agitated long: 16 strategies).
findings.F5: No weekday showed a next-day excess return with |t| above 1.44 over about 1,400 cases each.
findings.F6: The book is very sparse. It made 66 trades across folds B and C (mean net trade returns by year of +2.6 % to +7.2 %), and its 10 largest days carry 73 % of its summed daily return. Its weakness is how rarely the situation occurs, not the size of the move: the total move is 5.4 times the cost.

no_ideas: The tested idea's effect is confined to rising calm (F1), but its grading does not hold (F2). The other patterns that stand out either repeat the source brief (F3) or repeat rebounds the map already holds (F4). Nothing else stood out across profiles, the sign and size of the last day's move, volatility quartiles or weekdays (F5), so no new, ungraded-free idea is supported.
